podcast.body: Although not directly detailed as a Patty Smith original in this transcript, it's mentioned as her most covered song, indicating its significance. Later, 10,000 Maniacs' unplugged cover reached number 11 on the Hot 100 in 1994, two spots higher than Smith's original version had in 1978. "Dancing barefoot, its best known single would become Smith's most covered song after because the night."

podcast.body: Released in 1978, this song features co-writing credits between Patti Smith and Bruce Springsteen. Springsteen provided the music and chorus, but his work was stalled due to legal issues with his former manager, Michael Pell. Jimmy Iovine then gave a tape of the song to Smith, who, despite her usual meticulousness, wrote the rest of the lyrics in a single night while waiting by the phone for her future husband, Fred 'Sonic' Smith. Shirley Manson of Garbage hailed it as unusual and thrilling for a woman to so openly discuss lust, a theme typically reserved for male artists in the 1970s. "She labored over her lyrics because her songs are poetry and the words within them matter, all of which makes because the night even more incredible."

This remains Patti Smith's only top 40 single, indicating its significant commercial success compared to other releases like "Dancing Barefoot." "Because the night is the only top 40 single that Patty ever had."
